info.title: pi-worker B2
info.summary: Caller-to-worker API (B2) of nubl's pi-worker supervisor.
info.description:
HTTP/1.1 over a private Unix socket (`$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/pi-worker/b2.sock`, 0700 directory, 0600 socket).
There is no TCP listener. This document is the single source for the server's request and response
validators, the TypeScript types and the Go models (`npm run generate`).

Seeded from A0 (`prototype/a0` at `ee66117`, `openapi.json`). The method catalog is draft until P6
(contract revision 8, sections 4 onward); the behavioural invariants (sections 0, 0.1, 0.2) are frozen.

Extensions:
- `x-piw-mutation` (every operation): `true` when the operation changes state. A mutation's body
  requires `command_id`, a UUIDv7 (RFC 9562) the caller mints
  when it creates the command; a client never retries it; a
  failure after the request bytes are written is
  `effect: unknown`. A command id the worker may have admitted
  never runs again: past its retained receipt and expired id it
  is refused `command_id_beyond_retention`, `effect: no_effect`
  (see `receipt_expired_ids_max`).
- `x-piw-status: unsupported`: the server routes and validates the operation and answers `501` with
  `effect: no_effect`.
- `x-piw-event` (every event schema): the event manifest (type, producer, durability, visibility).
- `x-piw-body` (every operation): the request body mode. `json`: `application/json` only, at most
  `x-piw-json-max-bytes` (below) unless the operation declares a smaller `x-piw-max-bytes`, validated
  against its schema. `binary`: the declared media types only, streamed with a byte counter and refused
  at `x-piw-max-bytes`, which a binary operation must declare. `none`: no body. The router enforces the
  mode before any handler: a wrong content type is `415`, a body over the limit `413`, a body on a `none`
  operation `400`, all `effect: no_effect`.
- `x-piw-response` (every success response): `json`, `sse`, `ndjson` or `binary`. An `sse` response
  declares `x-piw-max-frame-bytes`, the most bytes one record may carry. An `ndjson` or `binary` response
  declares `x-piw-max-bytes` (the most body bytes) and its `headers`; the router validates the headers
  against their schemas, the content type against the declared media types and the length against the
  cap before anything is written, and an `ndjson` body must be complete lines, each one JSON value.

- `x-piw-grant-profiles` (in `info`): named method lists a grant can be registered with. `bridge` is
  exactly the methods of Shep's worker driver (`docs/plan/b2-for-shep.md` section 2.1); `npm run api:lint`
  fails if the two differ, and the Go fake's closure test needs a route and a wire fixture for each.

Named limit (invariant 8): private sockets and bearer grants do not isolate hostile code running as the
same OS user.

servers.description: HTTP over the worker's private Unix socket. The host name is not resolved.

List the workers this grant may see

post.summary: Create a worker (launch pi), optionally with its first prompt
post.description:
With `first_prompt`, one command and one receipt start a chat: once the
worker is ready the supervisor admits the prompt as the worker's first
execution, under the create's own `command_id`. The receipt names the
worker, and either the execution (`admission: accepted`, `execution_id`,
`disposition`) or the prompt's typed refusal (`admission: rejected`,
`error`) with the worker created and idle. See `FirstPrompt`. A grant
sends a first prompt only if it may also call `sessions.prompt`
(`grant_method_denied` otherwise), here and in `children.launch`.

post.summary: Change the bound session's model, thinking level or name
post.description:
A session write (contract 8.1): it names the binding it saw, is refused under a fence and while an
execution runs, and after its dispatch record a lost reply is `outcome_unknown` and fences the session.
At least one of `model`, `thinking` and `name`.

post.summary: Compact the bound session (pi's /compact)
post.description:
pi summarizes the session with its model and appends a compaction entry; live dialogs are cancelled at
their exact resolvers first. The binding does not move (same session file, same tree).
A session write: it names the binding it saw and is refused `no_effect` under a fence, during a binding
move and while an execution runs (`worker_busy`). Its dispatch record precedes the write to pi; after it,
only pi's explicit refusal before any change is `no_effect`, and a lost reply is `outcome_unknown` and
fences the session.

post.summary: Reload extensions, skills, prompts and context files (pi's /reload)
post.description:
The receipt reports the loader errors after the reload; the worker row's `resources` follow. Live dialogs
are cancelled at their exact resolvers first.
A session write: it names the binding it saw and is refused `no_effect` under a fence, during a binding
move and while an execution runs (`worker_busy`). Its dispatch record precedes the write to pi; after it,
only pi's explicit refusal before any change is `no_effect`, and a lost reply is `outcome_unknown` and
fences the session.

post.summary: Run an extension command (a slash command an extension registered)
post.description:
Only an extension command `commands.list` names with `invocation: commands.invoke`. A built-in that has
its own method (`/new`, `/model`, `/compact`, …) is refused `use_method` with the method in `detail`; any
other built-in, prompt template or skill is refused `unsupported_command`; an unknown name
`unknown_command`. All before any record.
A session write: it names the binding it saw and is refused `no_effect` under a fence, during a binding
move and while an execution runs (`worker_busy`). Its dispatch record precedes the write to pi; after it,
only pi's explicit refusal before any change is `no_effect`, and a lost reply is `outcome_unknown` and
fences the session.

post.summary: Send a prompt to the bound session
Queue a follow-up against a named execution
Steer the named running execution (delivered after its current turn)
Move the binding (new, fork, resume, navigate)
Bind a new session (pi's /new); the binding revision moves and the old binding is refused
Lift a fence with one disposition (keep, abandon, observed)
Stop the worker's pi; keeps the session and environment

200.description: Stop receipt with the observed termination.

post.summary: Relaunch pi on the same session after confirmed cleanup
post.description:
Starts a fresh pi process for a stopped or failed worker, in a new
cleanup domain at a new `worker_epoch`, and reopens the worker's
session file without prompting. The binding names the worker's last
generation. Refused `no_effect`, before anything is recorded or
started: `stale_binding`; `cleanup_pending_or_cleanup_unproven` unless
the previous epoch's domain was observed removed and that is recorded
(`cleanup: cgroup_empty_removed`), so a live or pending worker is
refused too; `session_fenced`, naming the uncertain command, until
`sessions.resolve_unknown`; `target_session_fenced`, naming it, while
another worker that bound the session since leaves it fenced;
`session_already_bound` or `exclusive_environment_already_bound`,
naming the holder, while another worker holds the session or the cwd;
`relaunch_session_unavailable` without a bound session or its file;
`child_relaunch_unsupported` for a child worker. The receipt names the
new binding. A launch that fails after the dispatch record cleans the
new domain. A spawn refused before any pi process existed, with that
domain observed removed, is `rejected` `no_effect` and may be retried.
Any other failure, and a stop, exit or fault that ends the launch while
it initializes, is `outcome_unknown` and fences the session (pi may
have run its switch hooks or opened it), durably before the reply,
until `sessions.resolve_unknown`.
Every earlier binding is stale afterwards, except the exact retry of a
`sessions.prompt` intent that a restart recovered and the owner kept
before this relaunch: it dispatches once on the first epoch a relaunch
brought up, until the binding moves or another relaunch runs.

post.summary: Cancel the current execution; allowed while fenced
post.description:
Drops the worker's queued input (intents end `no_effect`), cancels live dialogs at their exact resolvers, then
asks pi to clear its own queue and abort. Allowed while fenced, never lifting the fence. With `execution_id`,
only that execution is targeted: another one is `stale_execution`, and one that already settled is refused
`no_running_execution` (`no_effect`) before any record, so queued input stays and pi is sent nothing. Without
`execution_id` it targets whatever is current. A delivered receipt's `result`: `requested: true`;
`disposition`, from the execution that was current right before the abort and its state after pi's reply
(pi's abort waits for idle): `interrupted` when it had not settled and settled during the abort (this request
stopped it), `settled` when it had already settled before the abort was sent, `unknown` otherwise (no
settlement observed, or `profile: no_live_host` when no live pi was there to ask); when pi was asked,
`external_effects_stopped: unproven` (stopping a running tool's external effects is never claimed). A failure after the dispatch record is `outcome_unknown` with no
`result`; it is never replayed.

post.summary: Escape equivalent; allowed while fenced
post.description:
Drops the worker's queued input (intents end `no_effect`), cancels live dialogs at their exact resolvers, then
asks pi to clear its own queue and abort. Allowed while fenced, never lifting the fence. With `execution_id`,
only that execution is targeted: another one is `stale_execution`, and one that already settled is refused
`no_running_execution` (`no_effect`) before any record, so queued input stays and pi is sent nothing. Without
`execution_id` it targets whatever is current. A delivered receipt's `result`: `requested: true`;
`disposition`, from the execution that was current right before the abort and its state after pi's reply
(pi's abort waits for idle): `interrupted` when it had not settled and settled during the abort (this request
stopped it), `settled` when it had already settled before the abort was sent, `unknown` otherwise (no
settlement observed, or `profile: no_live_host` when no live pi was there to ask); when pi was asked,
`external_effects_stopped: unproven` (stopping a running tool's external effects is never claimed). A failure after the dispatch record is `outcome_unknown` with no
`result`; it is never replayed.

post.summary: Launch a child worker under the current execution
A child's claim to its parent (a claim, not proof)

get.summary: One interaction's recorded state and answer stage

post.summary: Answer an interaction if its binding and revision are current
post.description:
`answer_id_conflict` (409): the `answer_id` was already used for a
different answer. The request is refused before any record, so this
request had no effect, but an earlier answer under that `answer_id` may
have been recorded and applied. Resolve with `interactions.status` for
the interaction and `receipts.get` of the earlier command; never
re-answer.

get.summary: Page the bound session's pi entries
get.description:
Raw pi entries on the visible path from the session root to a
pinned watermark, oldest first. Without a watermark it pins the
worker's history marker: the newest entry on pi's selected path
that is in the session file (never an entry pi has not written;
a session with nothing written yet reads as an empty page). An
entry too large for a page is a `too_large` stub; read it with
`items.read`. History never creates a live interaction. A session's
raw lines by byte range, with or without a worker, are
`sessions.history`.

get.summary: Read one whole pi entry of the bound session
get.description:
The full entry a history page stubbed as `too_large`, up to
1 MiB of its raw line; a longer entry is refused
`entry_too_large`, `no_effect`. Image bytes are read with
`blobs.read` (P1-16).

post.summary: Read a file inside explicit confinement roots (sandboxed environments)
post.description:
A file of a sandboxed worker's root
(`launch_spec.environment.filesystem: bwrap`, P2-4), read through
opens pinned at that root with no symlink at any component. `path`
must lie inside one of `roots`, each inside the worker's root; no
component may be hidden (`.name`), `.` or `..`. Only a regular
UTF-8 file of at most 1 MiB. Refusals, all `no_effect`:
`files_read_requires_sandbox_environment` (an unsandboxed worker),
`explicit_roots_required`, `hidden_or_traversal_path_refused`,
`file_outside_explicit_roots`, `file_symlink_or_unavailable`,
`file_not_regular_or_over_1MiB`, `file_over_1MiB`, `file_not_utf8`.
The JSON reply escapes the content: at worst 6 bytes per content
byte (a control character's `\u0001` form) plus the escaped path and
envelope, under 6.1 MiB, within the clients' 8 MiB JSON response
limit.

post.summary: Owner-Git facts about a worker's checkout (saved launch pin)
post.description:
Facts about a sandboxed worker's Git checkout (P3-6), read by the
supervisor through owner Git (P2-6) with the Git pin the worker's
launch validated (memory only: a supervisor restart loses it) and a
private snapshot in the supervisor's state. The request names the
worker's current `worker_epoch` and the `commit` to inspect (and
optionally a `base`), each a full object id or a branch
`refs/heads/<ns>/<leaf>` in the worker's own namespace; never a
path, pathspec or option. The reply is facts, never an acceptance
verdict: the commit and its native tree (replacement objects off),
HEAD, the working tree's status, the paths changed from the base,
the pin's identity and the evidence's provenance. Lists are bounded
and say when they are truncated; the worktree state is judged on
the complete status. On a parent channel only the parent's own
children may be inspected. Owner Git runs in a child process with
its own process group, never on the supervisor's event loop, within
`hello.limits.artifact_inspection_budget_ms`, with at most
`hello.limits.artifact_inspections_max` inspections running
(`artifact_inspections_per_caller_max` per grant). The worktree
state fails closed on index state that hides tracked changes: an
index entry marked assume-unchanged or skip-worktree (detail
git_index_hides_changes), or a pinned `core.ignoreStat`,
`core.sparseCheckout` or `index.sparse` (detail
git_config_trusts_stat), refuses, never reads as clean.
Refusals, all `no_effect`:
`stale_binding` (`worker_epoch` is not the worker's current one),
`artifact_inspection_unavailable` (no saved launch pin: the worker
is not sandboxed in a linked worktree, or the supervisor restarted
since its launch; or owner Git refused the checkout or could not
run; `detail` names the reason),
`artifact_pin_mismatch` (the checkout's Git metadata is not the
saved launch pin), `artifact_ref_outside_namespace` (a ref outside
the worker's own branch namespace, or any ref of a detached
worker), `artifact_object_missing` (the commit, the base or the
commit's tree is not in the object store, or names no commit),
`parent_channel_requires_own_child` (on a parent channel, a worker
that is not the parent's child), `artifact_inspections_busy` (too
many inspections running, supervisor-wide or for this grant;
`detail` is supervisor_limit or per_caller_limit; nothing ran),
`artifact_inspection_timeout` (the inspection ran past its budget;
its owner-Git process group was killed).

put.summary: Stage one image for a later prompt (streamed binary upload)
put.description:
The body is the image bytes, streamed; it never goes through the JSON path. The worker counts bytes as
they arrive into a private staging file and refuses a body over `x-piw-max-bytes`
(`hello.limits.attachment_max_bytes`) with `413`, removing the file. The command and the worker travel
in headers; the session headers are recorded, and the prompt that uses the attachment checks its own
binding. After the last byte the SHA-256 must equal `Piw-Content-Sha256` and the magic bytes must match
the content type, else `400`, nothing staged. Then one journal record makes it `staged`.

Idempotent by `attachment_id` plus SHA-256 (Shep's S-4): the same id with the same hash returns a receipt
for the attachment already staged and stores nothing twice; the same id with another hash is refused
`attachment_id_conflict`. A failure after the request bytes are written is `effect: unknown`: read
`attachments.status` (or the receipt), never re-upload blindly. Allowed under a fence: staging writes no
session; the prompt that uses the attachment is refused.

parameters.name: Piw-Content-Sha256
parameters.description: Lower-case hex SHA-256 of the body.

get.summary: Read a staged attachment's state (after an upload whose reply was lost)
get.description:
`receiving` while its upload is still streaming (memory), `staged` once its journal record is durable,
`released` after `attachments.release` or after the prompt that used it was delivered. An unknown id is
never proof that nothing was staged: `unknown_attachment_is_not_proof_of_no_effect`, `effect: unknown`.

get.summary: List the sessions this worker catalog knows, newest activity first
get.description:
The sessions a worker of this supervisor has bound (the resume catalog), live or archived, up to
`limit` (at most 100) per call, filtered by `cwd` when given. A session is listed when its cwd is in the
grant's cwd scope and its last owner is in the grant's worker scope. `holder_worker_id` names the worker
holding it now ("open in"). Rows come from the session file; a file pi has not written yet reads as an
empty session.

get.summary: Read a session file's complete lines by byte range, with or without a worker
get.description:
Shep's shape (a) of `history.page` (question S-1): pi's session-file lines from byte `offset`, complete
lines only, ending on a line boundary, at most `max_bytes` unless one line alone is longer (then that one
line, up to `Piw-History-Line-Max`). It reads any session of the catalog, so an archived session reads by
`session_id` with no worker bound to it; scope is as for `sessions.get`.

Headers: `Piw-File-Identity` is stable across appends and changes when the file is replaced;
`Piw-Watermark` is the file's complete size (the byte after its last complete line), the value
`history.appended` carries; `Piw-Next-Offset` is where the next read starts; `Piw-Tail-Sha256` is the
SHA-256 of the last line read (with its line feed), to send back as `tail`; `Piw-Prefix-Sha256` is the
SHA-256 of every byte before `Piw-Next-Offset`, to send back as `prefix`.

Reset: send back `identity`, `tail` and `prefix` with the next `offset`. When the identity differs, the
line ending at `offset` is not the one `tail` names, or the bytes before `offset` are not the ones
`prefix` names (the file was replaced, shrank or was rewritten in place, including a rewrite followed by
an append, or one made while the supervisor was down), the worker reads from byte 0 and sets
`Piw-Reset: true`. The prefix is the check that survives a supervisor restart. Without `tail` or
`prefix`, an offset past the watermark is `history_offset_past_watermark` and one not on a line start
`history_offset_not_line_start`, both `400 no_effect`: a bad offset never reads as an empty page.

parameters.name: prefix
parameters.description: The `Piw-Prefix-Sha256` of the read that returned this `offset`.

Piw-Offset.description: The byte the body starts at (0 after a reset).

Piw-Prefix-Sha256.description: The SHA-256 of the bytes before `Piw-Next-Offset` (of no bytes when it is 0).

schema.description: pi's session-file lines, unparsed; B2 does not own their schema.

get.summary: The model catalog pi reports, for a worker or for a cwd before any worker exists
get.description:
Name exactly one of `worker_id` (the worker's pi process answers, with its current model and thinking
level) or `cwd` (a short-lived pi process loads that cwd's settings and resources, opens no session and
exits). `project_trusted` applies to `cwd` as it does to `workers.create`.
At most `hello.limits.inventory_probes_max` such processes run at
once, supervisor-wide; past it the call is refused
`inventory_probes_busy` (`no_effect`, retry later) before anything is
recorded or started.

get.summary: The slash commands pi offers, for a worker or for a cwd before any worker exists
get.description:
As `models.list` for `worker_id` and `cwd`. Each command says how it is invoked: an extension command
through `commands.invoke`; a built-in that has its own method (`/new`, `/model`, `/compact`, …) names
that method; anything else (other built-ins, prompt templates, skills) is `unsupported` and refused
explicitly.

post.summary: Release a staged attachment and remove its bytes
post.description:
The released record is durable before the bytes are removed, so no prompt can use them afterwards. Allowed
under a fence. A prompt that was delivered releases its attachments itself; the image stays in pi's
session file and `blobs.read` serves it from there.

get.summary: Read one image of a session entry as bytes
get.description:
The `index`-th image block of the entry, in document order, decoded from pi's session file: the image pi
stored (after its own normalization), so the photo card renders what the model got. Scope is as for
`sessions.get`. The media type must be in the image allowlist and match the bytes' magic, and the image
is at most `hello.limits.blob_max_bytes`; otherwise refused `no_effect`.

get.summary: Read a command's receipt without redispatch
get.description:
An unknown or expired command_id is never proof that nothing ran: an
unknown one is refused `unknown_command_id_is_not_proof_of_no_effect`
and an evicted one `receipt_expired`, both `effect: unknown`.

get.summary: One supervisor-wide SSE stream; a snapshot first on every attach
get.description:
Each SSE `data` field is one `EventFrame` as JSON. The worker never
replays: a reconnect gets a fresh `snapshot` whose `resync_reason` says
why. A stream ends with one `overflow` frame, then closes, in two kinds.
A resync (`resync_required: true`): its subscriber queue overflowed
(`subscriber_queue_overflow`) or a frame was invalid (`invalid_frame`);
the caller reconnects and resyncs from the new snapshot. A terminal end
(`resync_required: false`): the stream's authority ended (its grant
revoked, a parent channel's generation retired); `reason` is the refusal
code (`grant_revoked`, `parent_channel_retired`, ...), the frame is sent
before any later event, and the caller must not reconnect: a new
subscription is refused with that code, or, once a parent channel is
closed, finds no socket. A client ends its watch with that refusal
(`no_effect`), never with a resync. One SSE record (its field lines,
each with one line-ending byte) is at most 1 MiB (1048576 bytes); a
client reads lines of any length up to that cap and refuses a longer
record as `frame_too_large`, never truncating it.

parameters.name: worker_id
parameters.description: Comma-separated worker ids to filter on.

parameters.name: types
parameters.description: Comma-separated event types to filter on.

parameters.name: Last-Event-ID
parameters.description: The cursor of the last frame seen, as JSON.

bearerGrant.description: A per-caller grant registered by the owner; the worker stores only its hash.

FeatureWorker.name: worker_id
FeatureWorker.description: Ask this worker's pi process. Exactly one of worker_id and cwd.

FeatureCwd.name: cwd
FeatureCwd.description: Ask a short-lived pi process for this cwd. Exactly one of worker_id and cwd.

BadRequest.description: Malformed request (JSON, schema, parameters); nothing began.

Refused.description: Refusal; the `effect` field says whether anything began. Never implies cancel.

TooLarge.description: Request body over the advertised limit; nothing began.

UnsupportedMediaType.description: Request body media type is not one the operation declares; nothing began.

Unknown.description: Something may have happened; read the receipt, never retry blindly.

NotImplemented.description: The operation is in the catalog but not served by this worker yet; nothing began.

Effect.description: `no_effect`: the refused request began nothing. `unknown`: something may have happened.

detail.description: Human-readable detail. Never contains request values.

no_effect_evidence.description: Present only when a refusal after dispatch is `no_effect` (ProvenNoEffect).

major.description: A client refuses an unknown major.

pi_version.description: The pinned pi SDK version; null while no pi host is available.

named_limits.description: Stated limits of the guarantees (contract invariant 8).

attachment_max_bytes.description: The most bytes one `attachments.stage` body may carry.

attachments_per_message.description: The most attachments one `sessions.prompt` may reference.

attachments_total_bytes.description: The most attachment bytes one `sessions.prompt` may reference.

event_frame_bytes.description: The most bytes one `events.subscribe` SSE record may carry.

journal_max_bytes.description:
The supervisor journal never grows past this many bytes. Compaction
rewrites it to the retained records (each worker's and interaction's
latest record, retained receipts, expired command ids) before it
fills.

journal_control_reserve_bytes.description:
Journal room only control records may use: quota-exempt commands
(`workers.stop`, `executions.cancel`, `executions.interrupt`,
`sessions.resolve_unknown`, `children.report`,
`attachments.release`) and stop, exit,
fault, fence and recovery records. Before dispatch, an ordinary
command reserves room for every record it can emit (its receipts,
and its worker's rows, settlements and interactions); it is refused
`journal_result_capacity` (`no_effect`) when that room would reach
this reserve or the room every worker that may still be stopped
needs for its own stop and exit records. An ordinary record never
uses either.

ordinary_receipts_max.description:
The most receipts of ordinary commands retained. Receipts of
quota-exempt commands (`workers.stop`, `executions.cancel`,
`executions.interrupt`, `sessions.resolve_unknown`,
`children.report`) neither count toward this bound nor are refused
at it: they are retained beside it, bounded by
`journal_max_bytes`, and evicted like any other receipt. At the
bound the oldest evictable receipts are evicted: final, older than
`receipt_retention_min_seconds`, and not part of any pending
decision. Never evicted: an unresolved `outcome_unknown`, an
unfinished command, the command that created a worker, and a
command a worker's unsettled execution, fence, queue or child
lineage names. When nothing is evictable an ordinary command is
refused `receipt_capacity` (`no_effect`).

receipt_retention_min_seconds.description:
A final receipt is retained at least this long after its command
was created.

receipt_expired_ids_max.description:
How many evicted command ids the worker still remembers. Reusing
one, or reading its receipt, is refused `receipt_expired` with
`effect: unknown`: never run again, never proof that nothing ran.
An id evicted longer ago than this still never runs again (contract
rule "no replay past retention"): the worker keeps the newest issue
time of a forgotten UUIDv7 `command_id` and whether any other id was
forgotten, and refuses a command id it may have forgotten (a UUIDv7
not issued after that time, or any other id once one was forgotten)
`command_id_beyond_retention` with `effect: no_effect`, before any
record. Callers mint every `command_id` as a UUIDv7 (RFC 9562).

history_line_max_bytes.description: The longest single session-file line `sessions.history` returns.

inventory_probes_max.description:
The most inventory processes (`models.list` and `commands.list`
for a `cwd`) the supervisor runs at once, across every caller. A
process holds its slot until its cleanup domain is observed removed
and recorded: neither a client that disconnects nor a cleanup that
is not proven frees it (an unproven one frees it when recovery
confirms it). Past the bound the call is refused
`inventory_probes_busy` (`no_effect`) before anything is recorded
or started; the caller retries later.

artifact_inspection_budget_ms.description:
How long one `artifacts.inspect` may run. Owner Git runs in a child
process with its own process group, never on the supervisor's event
loop; past the budget the whole group is killed and the call is
refused `artifact_inspection_timeout` (`no_effect`).

artifact_inspections_max.description:
The most `artifacts.inspect` calls running at once, across every
caller. Past it the call is refused `artifact_inspections_busy`
(`no_effect`, `detail` `supervisor_limit`) before anything runs; the
caller retries later.

artifact_inspections_per_caller_max.description:
The most `artifacts.inspect` calls one grant (a parent channel's
own grant included) has running at once. Past it the call is
refused `artifact_inspections_busy` (`no_effect`, `detail`
`per_caller_limit`) before anything runs.

if_busy.description: What to do when an execution is running: `steer` it, queue a `follow_up` after it, or `reject` the prompt (`worker_busy`, `no_effect`). Absent means `reject`.

attachments.description: Staged images of this worker, sent as real image blocks with the text. At most `hello.limits.attachments_per_message` and `attachments_total_bytes` in total, else refused `no_effect`; not with `if_busy: steer`. The receipt's `result.accepted_images` is the number of images pi put in the message. A delivered prompt releases them.

Host.description: The SDK subprocess is the production host (plan section 1); RPC and ACP are not served.

resume_session_id.description: Reattach a session this worker catalog knows. Refused `session_already_bound`, naming the holder, while another worker holds or is opening it; `target_cleanup_unproven` while its last owner's cleanup is unproven; `target_session_fenced`, naming the uncertain command, while its fence is unresolved.

FirstPrompt.description:
A new worker's first input (`workers.create`): text only. Images go
with `sessions.prompt` once the worker exists (an attachment is staged
for a live worker). It has no command of its own: the first
execution's `command_id` is the create's, and the create's receipt
reports it.

- Admitted: the receipt is `delivered` with the worker (`worker_id`,
  `result`) and the execution (`admission: accepted`, `execution_id`,
  `disposition` as `sessions.prompt` reports it).
- Refused at admission by a check of `sessions.prompt` (a slash
  command): the receipt is still `delivered` with the worker, which is
  created, ready and idle, plus `admission: rejected` and the refusal
  code in `error`. No execution exists and nothing reached pi; the
  caller keeps the draft and may send it with `sessions.prompt`.
- Refused by pi before any input hook (busy or compacting): the same
  shape, `error` naming pi's refusal (`pi_refused_prompt: pi_busy`).
  The execution the dispatch record named is gone, so the final
  receipt has no `execution_id`.
- Uncertain: the execution id is in the create's receipt, durably,
  before any byte of the prompt reaches pi. A caller whose create reply
  was lost reads the receipt with `receipts.get` and never sends the
  create again; a duplicate `command_id` returns that receipt and never
  prompts twice. If pi's reply is lost the receipt is `outcome_unknown`
  with the worker, its `result` and the `execution_id`, and the new
  session is fenced on the create's `command_id` until
  `sessions.resolve_unknown`, also after a supervisor restart.

The text is never journaled (the receipt keeps only the request hash).

value.description: Text for input and editor, true or false for confirm.

actor.description: Opaque device or person reference supplied by the bridge; journaled with the outcome.

deadline.description: Absolute deadline, milliseconds since the Unix epoch.

ApprovalBinding.description:
A `tool_approval` card's approval: exactly what the worker's SDK
child binds the tool gate to (sdk-child `Approval` plus its
`gate_token`). The gate's release (`gate_check`) must repeat every
field but `gate_token` unchanged and before `expiry`. The supervisor
admits a card only with this whole object; any other field is
dropped, and a card without a valid binding is never shown (its
native dialog is cancelled, so the gate denies the tool).

digest.description: The extension's digest of the exact tool input.

expiry.description: Milliseconds since the Unix epoch; the gate denies at or after it.

gate_token.description: The child's id for this gate (a UUID); its terminal notification names it.

InteractionSummary.description: A pending native interaction not yet admitted as a typed interaction.

fenced_at.description: RFC 3339 time the worker latched this fence in its journal: the fence record's own timestamp, on the clock of receipt `created_at`. Set once; a later uncertainty or a partial resolution never changes it, and a restart keeps it.

GitPin.description: Launch-time Git pointer bytes of a sandbox root. Relaunch and owner Git commands refuse when any value changed.

WorkerFailure.description: Why a launch ended the row in status failed. The launch receipt keeps its own effect label.

status_since.description: RFC 3339 time the status last changed.

settle_count.description: Executions pi reported settled on this worker (finished-unseen on the phone).

recent_settlements.description: The worker's last settled executions, newest first, at most 8. Journaled with the row, so a subscriber that missed `execution.settled` (a disconnect, an overflow, a supervisor restart) recovers each settlement from the next snapshot. An execution appears once. The cap covers a reconnect gap of eight turns and keeps the row small in every snapshot, `worker.updated` and journal record; a `settle_count` gap larger than the list means some settlements are only in the session history.

repo_label.description: The name of the Git work tree holding the cwd, else the cwd's base name.

title.description: The session's display name (pi's session_info), set by `session.configure` or natively.

first_user_line.description: The first line of the session's first user text, without the worker's interrupt marker and trimmed, read from the session file as `preview` is (a title fallback). Null before pi wrote a user message with text. The worker cuts it to at most 280 UTF-16 code units, never inside a character. The schema's `maxLength` counts characters (Unicode code points), so it checks only the looser bound of 280 characters; a client must not rely on validation for the code-unit bound.

last_activity_at.description: RFC 3339 time of the newest entry in the session file.

settled_at.description: RFC 3339 time the supervisor recorded the settlement.

Lineage.description: A child names its parent; old and natively launched sessions are unknown, never roots.

Preview.description: The newest user or assistant text in the session file, without the worker's interrupt marker, at most 280 characters.

name.description: The command's name without the leading slash.

bytes.description: For `receiving`, the bytes received so far.

command_id.description: The `attachments.stage` command that staged it (or is staging it).

released_by.description: The command that released it (`attachments.release`, or the prompt that delivered it).

FileIdentity.description: Stable across appends to one session file; changes when the file is replaced.

models.description: Per-model usage and cost, from the assistant messages' own usage records.

holder_worker_id.description: The worker that holds the session now ("open in"); null when no worker holds it.

fenced.description: The last owner's fence is unresolved; resume is refused `target_session_fenced`.

invocation.description: How the command runs through B2: `commands.invoke`; `method`, the typed method in `method` (a built-in with its own operation); or `unsupported`, refused explicitly.

termination.description:
observed_stopped: normal stop, generation confirmed gone. superseded_generation_stopped: old generation
gone but a new relaunch was already running. superseded_generation_unknown: old generation cleanup
outcome unknown, new generation running. unknown: cleanup outcome unknown, generation status not checked.

bytes.description: The size of the entry's raw line in the session file.

ObjectId.description: A full Git object id (SHA-1 or SHA-256), lower case.

ArtifactRevision.description: A full object id, or a branch `refs/heads/<ns>/<leaf>`, which must lie in the worker's own namespace (the namespace of its pinned symbolic HEAD). Never an abbreviation, a revision expression, a path or an option.

status.description: The `git diff --name-status` letter, with a score for a rename or copy (`R100`).

from_path.description: For a rename or copy, the path it came from.

path.description: The rest of the porcelain line as Git prints it: one path, or `FROM -> TO` for a rename or copy, quoted by Git when it holds special characters.

ArtifactDiffDigest.description: Advisory digest of the diff from the base to the commit; never artifact identity.

commit.description: The subject (P2-6 `artifactSubject`) - the requested commit and its native tree.

ref.description: The branch the pinned symbolic HEAD names; null when HEAD is detached.

base.description: Present when the request names a base.

merge_base_id.description: The best common ancestor of base and commit; null when they share no history.

is_ancestor.description: The base is an ancestor of (or is) the commit.

changed.description: The paths changed from the base to the commit (`git diff --name- status`), in Git's order.

changed_truncated.description: More changes exist than `changed` lists (at most 10,000 entries and 1 MiB of paths).

worktree.description: The checkout's `git status --porcelain` (untracked files listed, ignored ones not). `conflicted` when any entry is unmerged, else `dirty` when any entry exists, judged on the complete status before `entries` is bounded.

truncated.description: More entries exist than `entries` lists (at most 10,000 entries and 1 MiB of paths).

pin.description: The saved launch pin the inspection compared, by identity.

sha256.description: SHA-256 of the pin's canonical JSON (keys sorted).

head_ref.description: The branch the pin's symbolic HEAD names; null when detached.

evidence.description: Owner Git (P2-6) on a private snapshot of the checkout's metadata, compared with the saved launch pin.

Cursor.description: Transport cursor. `transport_epoch` changes on every supervisor start and is independent of a worker's binding epoch.

EventFrame.description: One SSE frame. `type` selects the member.

SnapshotEvent.description: Sent first on every attach, at a synchronous barrier. `workers` is authoritative. No event replay.

OverflowEvent.description:
The last frame of a stream; the stream closes after it.
`resync_required: true`: the subscriber queue overflowed or a frame was
invalid (`reason` `subscriber_queue_overflow` or `invalid_frame`); the
caller reconnects and resyncs from a snapshot. `resync_required: false`:
the stream's authority ended (`reason` is the refusal code,
`grant_revoked` or `parent_channel_retired`); terminal, the caller does
not reconnect, and a client ends its watch with that refusal
(`no_effect`).

x-piw-event.notes: Two kinds. A resync overflow (queue overflow, invalid frame) carries resync_required true; the caller reconnects with resync=overflow. An authority end (grant revoked, parent channel retired) carries resync_required false and the refusal code as reason; it is terminal and is never followed by a reconnect.

resync_required.description:
True for a queue overflow or an invalid frame (reconnect and
resync); false when the stream's authority ended (terminal:
`reason` is the refusal code, never reconnect).

WorkerUpdatedEvent.description: The full worker row after a change.

SessionReboundEvent.description: The binding moved; mutations naming the old revision are refused.

action.description: The move. `native` when pi moved on its own and the worker cannot tell which move it was.

ExecutionSettledEvent.description: pi reported agent_settled for the execution (or pi handled the prompt without a turn). The frame is memory only; the settlement itself is journaled in the worker row's `recent_settlements`, which every snapshot carries.

FenceResolvedEvent.description: A fence was lifted. Resolving never claims an external effect was undone.

ChildReportedEvent.description: A child's report reached its durable receipt. A report is a claim, never proof; a `help` report never discharges the parent's launch fence.

InteractionsChangedEvent.description: The live interaction cards of a worker.

HistoryAppendedEvent.description: A worker's session file grew or was replaced. `watermark` is the file's complete size, the value `sessions.history` returns in `Piw-Watermark` for the same bytes.

ExecutionAdmittedEvent.description: The supervisor admitted an execution and journaled it, before the prompt reaches pi.

ExecutionStartedEvent.description: pi reported agent_start for the admitted execution; the row is journaled.

AssistantDeltaEvent.description: The assistant text pi is streaming (pi's `message_update` text deltas), memory only and never replayed. `tail` is the last at most 2048 characters of the message's text so far and `length` its full length: a client replaces its screen tail with `tail`, so a lost delta costs nothing. A subscriber whose transport is backpressured holds at most one undelivered delta per worker (a newer one replaces it), so a delta storm cannot overflow its queue.

ToolStartedEvent.description: pi started a tool call (`tool_execution_start`): the pending tool. Memory only, never replayed.

ToolFinishedEvent.description: pi finished a tool call (`tool_execution_end`). Memory only, never replayed.

ToolCallId.description: pi's tool call id (a longer one is cut to 512 characters, the same way in both events).

ToolSummary.description: One line about the call: the first of the arguments `command`, `path`, `file_path`, `pattern`, `url`, `query` or `description` that is a string, cut to 200 characters; null when there is none.

ReceiptUpdatedEvent.description: A receipt record of a worker's command was journaled (intent, dispatch, result, recovery). `receipt` is that record; read `receipts.get` after a gap.

FenceSetEvent.description: An uncertain command joined the worker's fence (the fence latched or its generation rose), after the fenced row was journaled. Session writes are refused until `sessions.resolve_unknown`. `fence.fenced_at` is when the fence first latched, not when this command joined it.

execution_id.description: The uncertain execution, when the uncertain command is the worker's execution.

command_id.description: The uncertain command that joined the fence.

AttachmentUpdatedEvent.description: An attachment's durable record changed (`staged` or `released`).
